title: GIVEN TO THE LORD AS COMMANDED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Moses gave the tribute to Eleazar the priest as the Lord's part, as the Lord commanded Moses. The half belonging to the Israelites, which Moses set apart from that of the fighting men—the community's half—was 337,500 sheep, 36,000 cattle, 30,500 donkeys and 16,000 people. From the Israelites' half, Moses selected one out of every fifty people and animals, as the Lord commanded him, and gave them to the Levites, who were responsible for the care of the Lord's tabernacle. - Num 31:41-47 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Twice in these verses we read the same refrain: "as the Lord commanded Moses." The tribute went to Eleazar as commanded; the portion went to the Levites as commanded. Everything was done exactly according to God's word. There is a beauty in this steady, unglamorous faithfulness — no shortcuts, no adjustments, just careful obedience to what God had said.

We sometimes imagine that obedience is only meaningful in dramatic moments. But most of the Christian life is made up of ordinary, faithful following of what God has already made clear. The soldiers had fought; now Moses simply did the quiet administrative work of dividing and giving, and he did it God's way. Faithfulness in the small, unnoticed tasks is still faithfulness, and God sees it.

This repeated obedience also points us to a greater Obedience. Where Israel so often failed to do as the Lord commanded, Jesus perfectly obeyed His Father in everything, even to death on a cross (Phil 2:8). His flawless obedience is credited to us who trust in Him. We are accepted not because our obedience is perfect, but because His was.

So we obey now not to earn God's favour but out of gratitude for the favour already given. Every quiet act of "doing as the Lord commanded" becomes a small act of worship, flowing from a heart made new by grace.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you as faithful in the quiet tasks as in the dramatic ones?
2. How does resting in Christ's perfect obedience free you to obey with joy?
3. What has God clearly asked of you that simply needs doing?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for Jesus, whose perfect obedience covers my failures. Help me to do as You have commanded in the small and quiet things, out of love for You. Amen.
